problem: Existing human-aware navigation simulators use crowd models that assign uniform behavior to all agents, restrict humans to point-to-point walking, are tied to deprecated ROS 1 or a single simulator, and ship small fixed metric sets, so fair evaluation of social navigation is hard.
motivation: Real-human experiments are costly and hard to reproduce, so simulation of realistic and diverse human behavior is essential for developing and evaluating social robot navigation. There is also no community consensus on metrics, so a flexible and extensible evaluator is needed.
key_idea: Extend HuNavSim (ROS 2) with Behavior-Tree nodes for rich human actions and conditions, noise-perturbed Social Force Model parameters, wrappers for several robotics simulators, and an RViz2-based scenario creation tool with an extended metrics suite.
insight: Combining a classical local model (SFM with sampled parameters) with modular Behavior Trees gives both trajectory variability and complex, event-driven multi-agent behaviors such as conversation formation and following. No quantitative ablation is reported; the evidence is a qualitative two-worker warehouse example. The simulator-agnostic wrapper design lets the same human behavior layer be reused across Gazebo, Isaac Sim and Webots.
method: Noisy SFM local navigation: Social Force Model (with group extension) whose force parameters can be default, user-specified, or sampled from normal distributions within ranges found by a sensitivity analysis.

Behavior Tree action/condition library: new nodes (GoTo, LookingAtPoint, StopAndWaitTimer, LookAtAgent, ConversationFormation, FollowAgent, ApproachRobot, SaySomething, isSpeaking, IsLookingAtMe, isAtPosition, etc.) composable into complex human behaviors, going beyond the six robot-reaction behaviors of v1.0.

Simulator wrappers: communication wrappers send agent states to the HuNavSim manager each step and apply the computed next state in Gazebo Classic, Gazebo Fortress, NVIDIA Isaac Sim and Webots, with example scenarios and robots.

RViz2 scenario creation panels: Qt panels (HuNavPanel, HuNavMetricsPanel) for placing agents, setting parameters, picking and assigning goals, exporting YAML plus auto-generated per-agent BT XML (Groot2 editable), and re-editing scenarios.

Evaluator and metrics: logs data and computes 28 metrics from v1.0 plus 4 new danger/surprise metrics from Singamaneni et al. (32 total); users select metrics and start/stop computation via ROS services.
Deployment: Docker containers and a CLI for installation and running examples.

setting.backbone: none (rule-based Social Force Model + Behavior Trees; no learned model)
setting.observation: simulator agent states (poses/velocities of humans and robot); 2D occupancy map for scenario creation
setting.action_space: human agent pose updates from SFM plus BT actions (GoTo, look, wait, follow, converse); robot controlled by the user's navigation stack (e.g., ROS Nav2)
setting.simulator: Gazebo Classic, Gazebo Fortress, NVIDIA Isaac Sim, Webots

numbers_note: No quantitative experiments; the paper is a tool description with a qualitative two-worker warehouse example.
results: The paper reports no benchmark numbers. It presents HuNavSim 2.0 as a ROS 2 tool working with four simulators, with 32 evaluation metrics and an RViz2 scenario generator, and demonstrates BT-driven behaviors qualitatively in an Isaac Sim warehouse.
limitations: No quantitative validation of the realism of noisy SFM or of BT behaviors against real human data.
Fortress support is still work in progress and lacks a provided robot; the local model is limited to classical SFM.
Scenario and BT creation is still manual; LLM/VLM-based generation is only future work.
